_findings: Published image (dcc-docling-serve-cu130:v1.35.0 with docling-glm-ocr 0.5.2 and docling-pp-doc-layout 0.2.5): all four configurations convert all 28 documents.

GLM-OCR is now about as fast as RapidOCR: 190 s for all 28 documents with the default layout (2'745 s with plugin 0.5.1) and 273 s with PP-DocLayout-V3 (2'701 s). The 30-page CELEX excerpt went from about 1'790 s to 92–102 s because born-digital pages are no longer sent to the VLM as full pages.

Output quality is unchanged where it was good: synthetic F1 0.94, handwritten note 96–97 %, phone photo handwriting 85–89 %. Precision against the text layer rose (0.82 → 0.85 default layout, 0.89 → 0.90 with PP-DocLayout-V3; Legislaturplan 0.83 → 0.96) because the hallucinated loops, HTML tables and code fences are gone.

The Legislaturplan's two text-free photo pages now come out empty with GLM-OCR, as with RapidOCR. One invention is left: with PP-DocLayout-V3, GLM-OCR describes the city photo on page 2 in one English paragraph (“This image presents an aerial view…”). The dashboard counts these photo pages as text pages only because earlier runs hallucinated on them, so the “empty pages” there are correct.
RapidOCR + PP-DocLayout-V3 is identical to the previous run at threshold 0.3, confirming 0.3 is now the plugin default.

Recommendation: RapidOCR + PP-DocLayout-V3 for printed documents, scans, plans and photos with printed text; GLM-OCR + PP-DocLayout-V3 when handwriting matters. GLM-OCR can still misread words in a way that changes the meaning, see the “Words not in reference” tab.
